tldr: DeepResearcher is a framework for end-to-end RL training of LLM-based deep research agents that interact directly with real-world web search, outperforming both prompt-engineered and RAG-based RL approaches.
contributions: Introduces DeepResearcher, the first comprehensive RL framework for end-to-end training of LLM agents in real web environments
Overcomes technical challenges of RL scaling with real web search including API rate limits, anti-crawling, network latency, and diverse webpage structures
Demonstrates substantial improvements over prompt-engineered and RAG-based RL baselines on open-domain tasks
Identifies emergent cognitive behaviors from end-to-end RL including planning, cross-validation, self-reflection, and honesty
methods: DeepResearcher uses Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to train a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbone model with outcome rewards (F1 score for correct format, -1 penalty for incorrect format). The system employs a multi-agent architecture with a dedicated web browsing agent that reads webpage segments sequentially and extracts relevant information into short-term memory. Training data consists of 80,000 QA examples curated from NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, and 2WikiMultiHopQA with contamination detection via pass@10 sampling. Technical challenges including rate limiting, anti-crawling, and high-concurrency requests are addressed through a 50-node distributed CPU server cluster, retry mechanisms, and search result caching.
results: DeepResearcher achieves up to 28.9 points improvement over prompt-engineered baselines and up to 7.2 points over RAG-based RL agents on open-domain research tasks. Evaluation spans in-domain benchmarks (NQ, TQ, HotpotQA, 2Wiki) and out-of-domain benchmarks (MuSiQue, Bamboogle, PopQA), with 512 examples sampled from most datasets and all 125 Bamboogle dev samples.
limitations: The reward mechanism uses F1 score which is suited for short-answer QA but may be insufficient for long-form answers, requiring more sophisticated reward mechanisms. The approach filters out time-sensitive, highly subjective, and potentially harmful questions from training data. Data contamination detection relies on pass@10 sampling from the base model, which may not catch all cases.
